questions.question: How did the telegraph work, and what is Morse code?
questions.expected_answer: The telegraph sent messages as pulses of electricity along wires hung on poles. An operator tapped a key to send signals, and an operator at the other end listened and wrote down the message. Morse code uses short signals (dots) and long signals (dashes) to stand for letters and numbers.

questions.question: What was a telegram, and why were telegrams short?
questions.expected_answer: A telegram was a message sent by telegraph. People wrote it on a form at the post office, it was sent by telegraph to the receiver's town and delivered by a messenger. Telegrams were short because people paid for every word.

questions.question: Who received a patent for the telephone, and how were early telephone calls connected?
questions.expected_answer: Alexander Graham Bell received a patent for the telephone in 1876. Early calls were connected by telephone operators at an exchange, who plugged cables into a switchboard to join the two lines. Later, automatic exchanges connected calls when people dialled or pressed buttons.
